scopeMarkdown:
Give gpux's `EditableText` the system keyboard, IME composition and native-feeling editing tools on iOS, Android and the web, including desktop and mobile browsers, plus an opt-in native field for credentials.

**Owner decisions (2026-10-16/17):**
- Fields stay drawn by gpux and talk to each platform's text-input protocol, the model Flutter and Compose Multiplatform use.
- Native text fields are an opt-in, for credentials only.
- The work is two epics, run one after the other in the `editable-text` worktree set (`~/.worktrees/editable-text/Gpux`, branch `feature/editable-text`). **`gpux-rich-editable-text` runs first.** This epic builds on its stored formatting and its per-row selection geometry.

## Starting point (origin/main 0eb1c1d)

**Android:**
- `PlatformInputHandler` is stored but never called (`crates/gpui_mobile/src/android/window.rs` ~1362).
- Text reaches apps only through the legacy global callback, fed by NativeActivity key events (`window.rs` ~1702-1755). There is no `InputConnection`, so Gboard's composition, swipe typing and voice cannot work.
- The keyboard is shown through the NDK `show_soft_input`, which ignores the keyboard type and exists only with `android-native-activity` (`jni.rs` ~1380-1408).
- The embedded host has no key or text events (`embedded.rs`).
- The clipboard becomes real in the first epic.

**iOS:**
- `GPUITextInputView` conforms only to `UIKeyInput` (`crates/gpui_mobile/src/ios/window.rs` ~308-452). It is 1×1 at (0,0).
- The keyboard appears only through `gpui_mobile::show_keyboard*`, and autocorrect is forced off.
- The legacy callback receives text before the input handler.
- There is no `UITextInput` or marked text, so no Japanese, Chinese or Korean composition.
- `IosWindow` implements none of `show_soft_keyboard`, `hide_soft_keyboard`, `text_input_state_changed`, `set_text_input_configuration` or `insets`.
- The keyboard height is kept in a global, not in `insets().ime`.
- The hardware-key FFI is never called.

**Web:**
- The hidden `<textarea>` IME mirror (`crates/gpui_web/src/ime_mirror.rs`) sits at (0,0), and `update_ime_position` is a no-op (`window.rs` ~1488).
- The keyboard appears on an editable tap (`events.rs` ~362-424).
- There are no selection handles or toolbar, and no IME inset.

**Core:**
- `TextInputConfiguration` has only autocorrect, autocapitalize, suggestions and the input action (`crates/gpui/src/platform.rs` ~2451).
- `EditableTextState` cannot set a configuration. It does not override `set_selected_text_range`, `text_length_utf16` or `text_input_editable_range`.
- `TextInputStateChange::{SelectionChanged, ContentChanged}` are never emitted.
- `invalidate_character_coordinates` is never called by `EditableText`.
- There is no general way to reveal a rectangle inside scrolling ancestors.

**Lanes:** the IME scene runs only in lanes A, B and C, because hosts cannot drive a platform's input method.

## Coordination with `gpux-a11y-devtools`

That epic is in progress on `feature/a11y-devtools`. It:
- moves to AccessKit 0.25, with the iOS and Android adapters;
- represents the focused editable node on the web through the IME mirror textarea (role, name, value, selection);
- adds `ScrollIntoView` ancestor scrolling.

**Rules for this epic:**
- Whichever epic merges second rebases.
- This epic keeps the a11y epic's IME-mirror contract. It reuses that epic's scrolling-ancestor mechanism when merged, and otherwise builds the shared one the a11y epic can call.
- Text-field accessibility stays in the a11y epic.

## Out of scope

- desktop IME changes (macOS, Windows TSF, Linux);
- RayX adopting the work, by mapping its field kinds to input configuration. That is RayX's own follow-up;
- spell-check UI;
- drag and drop of text on touch;
- bidirectional text.

## Owner-dependent acceptance

Real keyboards, IMEs, dictation and password autofill on devices and mobile browsers cannot be driven by the lanes. The owner runs them in the final sprint (`s08-owner-walkthrough`), recorded in `docs/measurements/text-input-walkthrough.md`.

## Defaults recorded instead of open product decisions

**Selection UI:**
- **iOS** uses UIKit's own selection UI (`UITextInteraction`).
- **Android and the web** share gpux-drawn selection handles. Android uses the platform floating toolbar (`ActionMode`); the web draws its own toolbar.
- **The magnifier** is Android-only.

**The native credential field:**
- It covers single-line username, password and one-time-code fields.
- The desktop falls back to `EditableText`.
constraintsMarkdown:
- **Input model.** Take Zed's input model unchanged. Touch editing uses `LongPressEvent`, `TouchDragEvent` and ordinary mouse events, and gpux additions sit beside the model (`gpui/input` rules).
- **Threads:**
  - Android View and IME calls run on the UI thread; editing runs on the GPUI thread.
  - UIKit calls run on the main thread.
  - Cross-thread state uses versioned mirrors, never blocking waits that can deadlock with the UI thread.
- **Platform rules:**
  - Keep the IME mirror `pointer-events: none`, and keep the clipboard and paste rules (`platform/web` rules).
  - Keep composition panels `FLAG_NOT_FOCUSABLE` except while text-taking content holds focus, and announce focus moves to Rust first (`platform/mobile` rules).
  - Java that gpux calls lives in `crates/gpui_mobile/java` under `dev.gpux.mobile`.
- **Legacy keyboard API.** The legacy `gpui_mobile` keyboard API keeps working for apps without an input handler: `set_text_input_callback`, `dispatch_text_input`, `show_keyboard*`, `hide_keyboard` and `keyboard_height`. A focused input handler receives text before the legacy callback.
- **Desktop is unaffected.**
- **Tests.**
  - Every behavior gets its own new test group: `crates/gpui/tests/<group>.rs`, a lane E or F check id, or a `tools/browser/specs` title prefix.
  - Sprint checks select exactly those groups.
  - Runtime proof runs in gpux's lanes; RayX checks are not gpux's proof.
- **Lane E** must build with and without `android-native-activity` (the embedded host is the default feature set).
- **Lane F** is the only proof for iOS runtime work.
- **Dependencies** come from crates.io only.

requirements.title: Input configuration and the shared input path
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: What a field asks of the keyboard, how platforms learn about app-driven changes, soft-keyboard Return, and keeping the caret visible.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**New configuration fields.** `TextInputConfiguration` gains:
- `keyboard`: text (the default), number, decimal, phone, email, url or search;
- `content_type`: none (the default), username, password, new password, one-time code, email, phone, url or name;
- `secure`: a bool.

The default stays the current default.

**State API.** `EditableTextState` stores a configuration through a setter and a getter, and its input handler returns it. A change while the field is focused reaches the platform in the same frame, through `Window`'s existing comparison.

**Secure fields** never get suggestions or autocorrect, whatever the other fields say.

New group `crates/gpui/tests/text_input_configuration.rs`.

**Input handler overrides.** `EditableTextState`'s input handler implements:
- `set_selected_text_range`: a platform-driven selection change lands clamped to character boundaries, makes no history entry, and keeps a marked range valid;
- `text_length_utf16`;
- `text_input_editable_range`.

**Notifying the platform.** When an `EditableText`'s text or selection changes, the window reports `TextInputStateChange::ContentChanged` or `SelectionChanged` to the platform, coalesced to once per frame. This covers changes from key bindings, programmatic setters, undo, paste and pointer selection. It never reports edits that came from the platform's own input handler calls.

**IME position.** When the caret's position on screen changes (an edit, a scroll, a layout change), `invalidate_character_coordinates` runs, so the platform's `update_ime_position` gets the caret rectangle.

New group `crates/gpui/tests/text_input_state_sync.rs`, using the test platform's recorded state changes.

**Return from a soft keyboard** arrives as a newline through the input handler:
- iOS `insertText("\n")`;
- Android `commitText` or `performEditorAction`.

It is first dispatched as the `enter` keystroke through the keymap, as the web already does with `insertLineBreak`. Only when nothing handles it does a multi-line field insert a newline; a single-line field inserts nothing.

**Hardware Enter keys are unchanged.**

New group `crates/gpui/tests/text_input_soft_return.rs`.

requirements.title: iOS: UITextInput, the keyboard and UIKit's editing tools
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The iOS window speaks UITextInput for the focused field and lets UIKit draw its own editing tools.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Hardware keyboards.** The input view's `pressesBegan:` and `pressesEnded:` dispatch `KeyDown` and `KeyUp` to GPUI, with modifiers and repeat, so arrows and shortcuts work. Printable characters still arrive exactly once, through `insertText`.

**Keyboard inset.**
- `UIKeyboardWillChangeFrame` updates `insets().ime`. It is zero when the keyboard is hidden or floating.
- `on_insets_changed` fires, and `visual_viewport_bounds` excludes the keyboard.
- `keyboard_height()` keeps working.

**Tests:**
- lane F check `text-input-ios-keys` calls the press handler with the key codes and modifier flags UIKit delivers (the Objective-C method is a thin forwarder);
- lane F check `text-input-ios-inset` shows the software keyboard on the Simulator, with the hardware keyboard disconnected by the testkit, and asserts the inset and the reveal.

requirements.title: Android: InputConnection, the keyboard and hardware keys
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The focused field gets a real InputConnection on both Android hosts.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**The host view.** A gpux Java view in `dev.gpux.mobile` hosts an `InputConnection` for the focused `EditableText`, in both the NativeActivity host and the embedded host.

**Focus and the keyboard:**
- Focusing an editable field gives that view the window focus. The move is announced to Rust first, so GPUI does not pause.
- The soft keyboard is shown through `InputMethodManager.showSoftInput`.
- It stays up across fields and hides on blur.

**`EditorInfo` comes from the configuration:**
- the `inputType` class, variation and flags: text, number, decimal, phone, email, uri, password and visible password; no suggestions; capitalization; multi-line;
- the `imeOptions` action, plus `IME_FLAG_NO_PERSONALIZED_LEARNING` for secure fields;
- the initial selection.

**Test:** lane E check `text-input-android-keyboard`. Focusing a field shows the keyboard (reported by the input method service), the `EditorInfo` matches the configuration, and GPUI stays active.

requirements.title: Web: the IME mirror at the caret and keyboard hints
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The browser's input method and virtual keyboard follow the focused field.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Mirror placement.** `update_ime_position` places the IME mirror textarea at the focused field's caret rectangle, with the field's font size. It stays transparent and `pointer-events: none`. As a result:
- desktop IME candidate windows open at the caret;
- mobile browsers scroll the visual viewport to the field, not to the page top.

On blur it returns to its idle place.

**a11y contract.** It keeps the a11y epic's role, name, value and selection contract when that is present.

**Test:** `tools/browser/specs/text-input.spec.ts`, titles `text-input: mirror ...`. They compare the mirror's box with the caret after focus, typing and scrolling.

requirements.title: Touch editing on Android and the web
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Touch selection handles, an edit toolbar and the Android magnifier for gpux-drawn fields.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**Touch gestures,** on touch input only. Mouse input keeps today's behavior, and iOS uses UIKit (IOS-3):
- **Tap:** places the caret.
- **Long press:** selects the word under it, or shows the toolbar with Paste in empty text, and shows two selection handles.
- **Double tap:** selects the word.
- **Dragging a handle:** moves that end of the selection. Handles swap rather than cross, and the field auto-scrolls at its edge.
- **Tapping the caret handle:** toggles the toolbar.

**Drawing the handles:**
- They paint in the overlay (deferred), above other content and outside the field's clip.
- They use the selection color, with a touch target of at least 44 points.
- They hide while typing and on blur.
- They are placed from the per-row selection geometry.

New group `crates/gpui/tests/editable_text_touch.rs`, with simulated touches on the test platform.

**Android magnifier.** While a handle or the caret is dragged, `android.widget.Magnifier` shows the text around it, and hides on release. Below API 28 there is no magnifier, and no error.

**Test:** lane E check `text-input-android-magnifier`.

requirements.title: Opt-in native credential field
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: A single-line native field for usernames, passwords and one-time codes, so platform autofill and password managers work.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
**The element.** `native_text_field` (gpux core), with a `NativeTextFieldState` entity:
- Value changes, focus and submit (Return) sync both ways.
- The content type, secure flag and keyboard come from `TextInputConfiguration`.

**Platform hook.** Platforms create the native control through a `PlatformWindow` hook. When there is no native control, the desktop included, the element renders an `EditableText` (masked when secure).

New group `crates/gpui/tests/native_text_field.rs`: the state API and the fallback on the test platform.

**iOS.** A `UITextField` in a window-composition native surface, placed at the element's bounds intersected with its content mask, hidden when the element is not placed, and removed when dropped.
- `textContentType`, `secureTextEntry`, the keyboard type and the return key come from the configuration.
- Font, color and placeholder come from the element's text style.
- gpux overlays draw above it.

Lane F check `native-field-ios`.

**Android.** An `EditText` in a composition platform-view panel.
- It is focusable while touched, by the existing rule.
- `autofillHints` and `inputType` come from the configuration.
- Font, color and hint come from the text style.
- It has the same placement and disposal as platform views.

Lane E check `native-field-android`.

**Web.** An `<input>` inside a `<form>` in the `html_element` DOM overlay, with DOM-owned input.
- `autocomplete`, `type="password"` and `inputmode` come from the configuration.
- Its styles come from the text style.
- `gpui_web` creates and syncs it, value and events included, without trusted HTML strings.

Lane B titles `native-field: ...`.
